name: antepartum hemorrhage overview
title: Bleeding in the second or third trimester: after the mother and fetus are assessed and non-obstetric sources and labour are ruled out, pain and whose blood it is separate placental abruption (edge or concealed), placenta previa, the placenta accreta spectrum and vasa previa; each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order, and a panel sets delivery by gestation

root.title: Bleeding in the 2nd or 3rd trimester: is it PAINFUL, and WHOSE blood is it?
lines: every one: airway, breathing, circulation for mom (oxygen + intravenous access if unstable) · non-stress test (NST) for the fetus
stat: complete blood count · international normalized ratio (INR), partial thromboplastin time (PTT), FIBRINOGEN · creatinine · group and screen
rule out first: non-obstetric (hemorrhoids, varices, bladder infection, stones → treat the cause) and LABOUR (a dilating cervix bleeds: 'show')

groups.title: PAINLESS: where is the placenta?
lines: maternal blood · placental site from the anatomy scan

head: h
Placental abruption
premature separation of the placenta from the uterus
most at 35–38 weeks, any gestation
pres: NO bleeding · severe pain · fetal distress
inv: once the other sources are ruled out

head: h
Placenta previa
implanted over, or within 2 cm of, the internal os
complete: covers it · marginal: within 2 cm
pres: • fetus stable unless the mother is not
inv: found at the 18–20 week scan; many move clear by the 3rd trimester
ANY cervical change can start a SUDDEN, SEVERE bleed
tx: no myometrium to clamp the vessels: shock, coagulopathy, hysterectomy

head: h
Placenta accreta spectrum
accreta · increta · percreta
placenta INVADES the uterine wall
pres: myometrium cannot contract over the invaded site
inv: 1 · Ask: previous cesarean or uterine surgery?
the scar lacks a full endometrial cover
tx: unless the invasion is very focal

head: h
Vasa previa
unprotected FETAL vessels cross the cervix or lie within 2 cm
pres: a tiny volume is a lot of the fetus's blood
inv: fetal blood in the VAGINAL bleed

panels.title: Every bleed: mother and fetus, then GESTATION decides
items: ≥ 35–36 weeks: DELIVER · induction if mother and fetus are reassuring, cesarean section if not

PRETERM + active bleed: birthing unit, continuous fetal monitoring · steroids + magnesium sulfate (see the PRETERM LABOUR chart) · neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) or tertiary consult if < 28–32 weeks · bloods every 4–6 h
PRETERM, stable, bleeding settled: antenatal ward · NST, growth + placental ultrasound, periodic bloods
the danger: CONSUMPTIVE COAGULOPATHY · the placental bed's huge flow uses up platelets and clotting factors
